nodes.description: Constant state variable holding the first hardcoded payout address 0x4135cfC4559df9145479010B7E21C7449fC9CfdE used by withdraw().
Constant state variable holding the second hardcoded payout address 0xDfd67f52D72e5ACFb42e53dB30E633F0Da8bE130 used by withdraw().
Public uint256 mint price, initialized to 0.05 ether, read by fallback() and written by set_price().
Public uint256 hard cap of 2100 tokens enforced by fallback() before incrementing totalSupply.
Public uint256 counter of minted tokens, incremented in fallback() and overwritten by set_total_supply().
fallback() external payable mint entry point: checks msg.value against price, checks totalSupply against maxSupply, derives amount from msg.value and increments totalSupply.
Owner-only setter that writes the newprice parameter into the price state variable.
Owner-only setter that overwrites the totalSupply state variable with the val parameter.
Owner-only function that performs two external value transfers using address(this).balance and the truncated division balance/6.0.
Access-control modifier 'own' that requires msg.sender to equal the hardcoded owner address 0x5e0a744f101F82E0a661477E36783C6c22d3D791.
Caller-controlled address used as the ownership check in modifier own and emitted in the Minted event by fallback().
Caller-supplied uint256 parameter of set_price() that becomes the new mint price.
Caller-supplied uint256 parameter of set_total_supply() that becomes the new totalSupply.
Local uint256 in fallback() derived from msg.value (1..5) and added to totalSupply.
External value transfer payable(to).transfer(address(this).balance / 6.0): hardcoded recipient plus truncating integer division of the contract balance.
External value transfer payable(to1).transfer(address(this).balance) draining the remaining contract balance to a hardcoded address.
State update totalSupply += amount executed after only a pre-increment check totalSupply < maxSupply, allowing the cap of 2100 to be exceeded.

edges.reason: msg.sender is compared against a hardcoded owner address inside the own modifier, gating every privileged function.
fallback() uses msg.sender as the minter address emitted in the Minted event.
set_price() is guarded by the own modifier, restricting price changes to the hardcoded owner.
set_total_supply() is guarded by the own modifier, restricting supply overwrites to the hardcoded owner.
withdraw() is guarded by the own modifier, restricting fund extraction to the hardcoded owner.
fallback() reads price in require(msg.value >= price) to validate the sent value.
fallback() reads maxSupply in require(totalSupply < maxSupply) to bound minting.
fallback() reads and updates totalSupply when minting, allowing the counter to be pushed past maxSupply.
fallback() branches on msg.value to assign the local amount value between 0 and 5.
Local amount flows into the totalSupply += amount state update only when amount > 0.
The unchecked-vs-cap supply update writes the new value into the totalSupply state variable.
The newprice parameter is consumed by set_price() as the value to store.
set_price() writes the supplied newprice into the price state variable.
The val parameter is consumed by set_total_supply() as the value to store.
set_total_supply() overwrites the totalSupply state variable with val.
withdraw() performs an external value transfer to the hardcoded address to with a balance/6.0 amount before any supply/accounting reconciliation.
withdraw() performs a second external value transfer to the hardcoded address to1 using the remaining contract balance.
withdraw() reads the constant address to as the destination of the first transfer.
withdraw() reads the constant address to1 as the destination of the second transfer.

normalization_plan.reason: The newprice parameter has no independent behaviour and only exists as the input written into price by set_price(), so it should be merged into that function node.
The val parameter has no independent behaviour and only exists as the input written into totalSupply by set_total_supply(), so it should be merged into that function node.
The local amount is only used to compute the totalSupply increment, so it should be merged into the supply_update unsafe_operation that performs the mint accounting.
